summary.headline: NIIT Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR957 million and EBITDA loss narrowed to INR14 million from INR63 million.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR957 million, up 14% YoY, with enterprise up 8% to INR618 million and consumer up 27% to INR339 million. Operating expenses grew 7%, narrowing EBITDA loss to INR14 million from INR63 million a year earlier. PAT rose 85% YoY to INR81 million, helped by INR180 million net other income, mostly treasury income. Management guided to double-digit YoY revenue growth and near-breakeven EBITDA in Q2 FY27, with positive margins in H2.

financial_highlights.change: vs negative INR63 million in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.commentary: Revenue INR618 million, up 8% YoY; enterprise tech training INR498 million, up 16% YoY, driven by upskilling of lateral roles while fresher onboarding stayed volatile.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR339 million, up 27% YoY; consumer tech INR182 million, up 15% YoY. Enterprise-to-consumer mix moved to 65-35 from 68-32 a year ago.

segments.name: Technology (product lens)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR680 million, up 16% YoY. Management said StackRoute and RPS, now merged as enterprise technology learning solutions, performed well.

segments.name: BFSI and other (product lens)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR277 million, up 9% YoY, helped by stronger fresher hiring at partner banks while lateral training stayed under pressure. Banking, TPaaS and service excellence training combined into BIPS, which also performed well.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: double-digit YoY revenue growth expected.
Q2 FY27: EBITDA near breakeven, positioning for positive margins in H2 FY27.
FY27 vs FY26: stronger revenue growth, improving margin and continued order intake momentum expected.
Capex is past its peak in the current investment cycle and expected to moderate.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was INR66 million; management says peak platform investment has passed.
Employee count was 866 at end-Q1, down 65 QoQ and down 19 YoY.
Cash and cash equivalents of INR7,231 million support investment through the cycle.
Four new BFSI solution lines (insurance, NBFC, wealth, Gen AI) are live with more than 15 clients.
Inorganic opportunities are being evaluated for capabilities, channels or IP with a clear path to returns and cash return.
demand_pricing: AI programs contribute about 9% of total revenue; AI-led training carries higher realisation but smaller batch sizes, per CEO.
Order intake of INR953 million in Q1, cited as continuing strong.
BFSI onboarding demand showing early recovery, while L&D budgets at large private banks remain constrained.
Competition is intensifying from IIT/IIM and other programs; management is differentiating on outcome-based training rather than completion or credentials.
AI engineering teams at GSIs and GCCs run 40% to 70% smaller; one engagement cut a planned 150-person team to 42.

qa_highlights.question: How do pricing realisations and ARPU for AI-led training compare with legacy IT training?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-led training has higher realisation, but batch sizes are smaller because advanced courses need coding and Python prerequisites.

qa_highlights.question: What is the early career vs WorkPro learner split in consumer, given the enrolment dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer tracks the split because the lines are fuzzy. Early career mix is rising but below expectations given muted hiring; iamneo's university offerings performed well.

qa_highlights.question: Is consumer growth driven by experienced professionals, and how are StackRoute and TPaaS performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is led by 2-3 year experienced professionals reskilling in AI. StackRoute and RPS are now combined as enterprise technology learning solutions; TPaaS sits in BIPS. Management said both performed well, but separate figures are no longer reported.

qa_highlights.question: How is NIIT positioned against the growing number of IIT/IIM and other AI certification offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it differentiates on outcomes and capability demonstration rather than credentials, though consumer awareness of this is still low.

qa_highlights.question: Has the integration of StackRoute and RPS improved go-to-market?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said the two are complementary (OEM-specific training versus long-term solutions) with GSI-heavy and GCC-heavy customer bases. Integration is ongoing, and the merger took effect 1 July.

qa_highlights.question: Has the macro improved since last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the macro is essentially unchanged and no firm direction is visible. It is focusing on AI opportunities and spreading risk across new segments and inorganic growth.

risks_watch: Fresher onboarding demand at corporates has not yet recovered; onboarding recovery is still early.
BFSI L&D budgets at large private banks remain constrained.
Competitive pressure from IIT/IIM and other AI programs; consumer awareness of outcome-based positioning is low.
Segment reporting has been consolidated after the RPS and IFBI merger, so StackRoute and TPaaS figures are no longer disclosed separately.
Exceptional expenses of INR15 million related to a legacy tax matter and the amalgamation scheme.
Q2 EBITDA target is only near breakeven, so the H2 margin turn depends on delivery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI and technology growth and on the path to positive margins, but cautious on macro and BFSI L&D budgets. Management avoided giving quantified macro views and did not give numbers for StackRoute or TPaaS after the merger.
key_quotes: Order intake continued to remain strong, indicating our investments in the new AI programs as well as our go-to-market initiatives.
In Q1 FY '27, NIIT moved beyond its banking anchor to activate four new solution lines across insurance, NBFC, wealth and Gen AI.
We expect double-digit revenue growth year-on-year in Q2 FY27.
It is the capability which counts rather than the credential.

adds.what: Four new BFSI solution lines (insurance, NBFC, wealth, Gen AI) already live with more than 15 clients

growth.why: Management guides Q2 FY27 double-digit YoY revenue growth and near-breakeven EBITDA, with stronger FY27 revenue growth and improving margins vs FY26, backed by Q1 order intake of INR953 million and four live BFSI solution lines, though no quantified capacity additions or revenue target were given.
